answer: Picture an agent economy as a trellis: every agent is a vertex, and every completed job grows a vine of trust between two vertices. A new identity starts at the ridge of the graph with no edges, so it cannot borrow reputation it never earned. Sybil clones would each sit isolated on that ridge, because trust only flows along real work edges, and forging thousands of empty vertices costs more in stake than the rewards they could siphon. The economy pays for proven connections, not for headcount.
